narrative.overview:
A warm sheet of paper with graphite type on it, and a few pastel stages set into it where the real device turns. Everything that is not product footage holds still. The type does the structural work: large Archivo headlines at weight 500, pulled tight, with the second half of the opening line stepping back to a softer grey. Hairlines divide the page. There are no panels, no gradient fields, no icon grids.

The world was set by the October 2026 landing page (`client/src/routes/+page.svelte`, notes in `docs/landing-2026.md`) and extended unchanged to the eighteen guide pages under `/mockups`, `/use-cases` and `/alternatives` (`client/src/lib/components/guides/`). The two surfaces declare the same custom properties separately: the landing scopes them under `.landing`, the guides under `.guide` in `guides.css`. Neither stylesheet reaches the studio at `/platform`. Where the two surfaces differ, this file says so.

Density is generous at the top and tightens below. A first viewport holds one headline, one short lead, one rust button with a proof line under it, and a stage. Further down, hairline lists, a two-column FAQ and a closing "Let's see it." carry the rest.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper (`paper`) and graphite ink (`ink`), one rust accent (`rust`) for the primary action and active marks.
Archivo only, weights 400 to 600, display tracking between -0.04em and -0.07em.
Courier New only for measurements: loop seconds, counts, ordinals.
Pastel stages whose ground is the preset's own `previewBackground`.
Hairline rules instead of boxed cards. Flat surfaces.
Only product footage moves. UI motion is 160ms state feedback.

rules.name: The One Rust Rule
rules.body: Rust is used for the primary action and active marks only. Never for headings, body text, backgrounds or decoration. A screen carries one or two rust buttons (top and close), never a row of them.

rules.name: The Footage Owns The Colour Rule
rules.body: The pastels belong to the motion presets. A stage's ground is the preset's `previewBackground`; do not invent a new pastel for a surface, and do not use the pastels on UI chrome.

rules.name: The Tight Display Rule
rules.body: Headlines are Archivo 500 with negative tracking that grows with size: -0.04em around 30px, -0.055em around 50px, -0.06em to -0.07em at display sizes. Line height drops below 1 at display sizes (0.97 to 0.99). H1 and H2 use `text-wrap: balance`; paragraphs use `text-wrap: pretty`.

rules.name: The Measuring Tape Rule
rules.body: Courier New appears only for numbers that measure: seconds, pixels, counts, ordinals. Never for prose, labels or headings.

rules.name: The Step-Back Headline Rule
rules.body: On the landing the hero's second line ("Every angle.") is set in soft ink. The guide H1s apply this deliberately: everything after the first comma steps back to soft ink ("Free iPhone 16 Pro mockups, *in motion.*"). A headline without a comma stays fully ink. Display headlines only.

rules.name: The Shared Column Rule
rules.body: Everything aligns to the one container and its gutters. Stages and lists run to its edges; nothing bleeds to the viewport except the paper itself.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Stages, cards, tiles, lists and buttons have no shadow at rest or on hover. Depth is a change of ground, not a lift.

rules.name: The Only Footage Moves Rule
rules.body: Nothing enters, fades in, parallaxes or animates on scroll. The only motion is the product's own footage, plus 160ms state feedback: colour, background, a 0.98 press, the 180° menu arrow, the guides' 3px arrow nudge and their 320ms stage-ground change.

rules.name: The Reduced Motion Rule
rules.body: Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, every transition is removed, the press scale is removed, and previews wait for a tap.

rules.name: The 44px Rule
rules.body: Every link and button is at least 44px tall or wide: header links, selectors, filters, breadcrumbs, text links, round links, playback. Mobile menu rows are 48px. The guide footer's link columns break this rule (hub links 32px, guide links 30px tall) and are not a precedent.

rules.name: The Fine-Pointer Hover Rule
rules.body: Hover colours and backgrounds are declared only inside `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`. Touch screens get press feedback, not stuck hovers.

rules.name: The Rust Focus Rule
rules.body: Keyboard focus is a 2px rust outline offset 5px on every link and button (`:focus-visible`). MotionPreview's control is the exception: an ink outline 3px out. A skip link ("Skip to content") slides in on focus.

dos: **Do** set every new marketing surface on `paper` with `ink` text and `hairline` dividers, scoped under its own root class like `.landing` and `.guide`.
**Do** keep rust to the primary button, the wordmark square, active marks, link hover and focus.
**Do** show the product's own footage first, on a stage whose ground is the preset's `previewBackground`, with its loop length in mono.
**Do** set headlines in Archivo 500 with the tight tracking of the hierarchy above, and let only display headlines step back to `ink-soft`.
**Do** name what the primary button opens, and point it at `/platform/animation/<motion>` for the motion on show.
**Do** separate sections and list rows with 1px hairlines, and keep cards to media plus a title row.
**Do** keep every target at 44px or more, gate hover on `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`, press at scale 0.98 and transition over 160ms.
**Do** honour `prefers-reduced-motion` by removing transitions and leaving previews on their poster until tapped.
donts: **Don't** use rust for headings, body text, section backgrounds or decorative fills.
**Don't** invent pastels; a stage or tile takes its preset's ground.
**Don't** set prose, labels or headings in Courier New; it is for measurements only.
**Don't** add entrance, fade-in, parallax or scroll-driven animation; only product footage moves.
**Don't** box content in bordered or shadowed cards, or lift anything with a shadow on hover.
**Don't** add icon grids, stock heroes, testimonials, ratings, logos or counts the product does not have.

**Don't** set a small label above a section heading. The landing's `section-index` lines ("The motion library / 16", "Got something to show?") predate this file and are not a pattern; the guides ship without them.
**Don't** copy MotionPreview's pill shape or Arial label into other controls.
